description: A button triggers an immediate action, such as submit, confirm, open or delete.

mapping.note: Slot: shown when an element is passed.
Slot: shown when an element is passed.

paragraphs: A button triggers an immediate action, such as submit, confirm, open or delete.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: A button triggers an immediate action in the current context — submitting a form, confirming a choice, opening something or deleting an item. Four emphasis levels (Primary, Secondary, Ghost, Danger) keep the most important action on a screen the easiest one to find.
Use buttons for actions only. If activating it takes the user to another page or location, it is navigation and must not be a button.

sections.heading: When to use
paragraphs: •   To let users submit, confirm, open or delete something immediately.
•   To mark the single most important action in a context — Primary.
•   To offer supporting actions of lower weight next to a primary one — Secondary or Ghost.
•   To trigger destructive or irreversible actions such as delete or remove — Danger.

sections.heading: When not to use
paragraphs: •   When the action navigates to another page or location — use a text link instead.
•   Don't use Danger styling for actions that aren't destructive — use Primary, Secondary or Ghost.

sections.heading: Anatomy
paragraphs: •   ① Container — the interactive wrapper; owns variant, size and state.
•   ② Icon (optional) — leading or trailing, never both. Vertically centred with the label. Decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology.
•   ③ Label — text describing the action. Required unless the button is icon-only.
Not shown: the loading indicator that replaces the leading slot while is-loading is on. It is not built yet.

sections.heading: Sizes
paragraphs: Dense UIs, toolbars and table rows.
The default size for most buttons.
Primary page calls to action and touch-first screens.
Every variant shares the same size scale. Each size defines its own height, horizontal padding, font size and icon size.

sections.heading: Alignment
paragraphs: Content is always centred horizontally and vertically. The icon sits on the side set by the icon property and is vertically centred with the label; the icon–label gap is the same across variants.
Label hidden with Show label = off. Must have an accessible label (aria-label).

sections.heading: Placement
paragraphs: Buttons hug their content within the size's padding and are not stretched. A full-width option (container spans its parent, content stays centred) is defined in the component skill but not exposed as a Figma property yet.
Use one primary action, paired with lower-emphasis actions.
Don't place two primary buttons in the same context — they read as equally important.
Keep every button in a group the same size.
Don't mix sizes in one group.
Use Danger only for destructive or irreversible actions.
Don't use Danger styling for a non-destructive action.

sections.heading: Main elements
paragraphs: •   Use a verb that describes the action, e.g. Save, Delete, Open.
•   Required on every button unless it is icon-only.
•   Optional — leading or trailing, never both.
•   Decorative icons must be hidden from assistive technology.
•   Icon-only buttons must have an accessible label (aria-label).

sections.heading: States
paragraphs: A button has no persistent on/off state: it runs its action and returns to rest. Every variant starts in the Default state.
•   Hover — the pointer is over the button.
•   Pressed — during a press; gives immediate visual feedback so the press registers.
•   Focused — keyboard focus; always shows a visible focus indicator.
•   Loading — action in progress. Defined in the skill but not built yet.
See the Style tab for how each state looks.

sections.heading: Interactions
paragraphs: Clicking anywhere on the button runs its action. Disabled buttons ignore clicks. While a button is loading, repeat clicks are ignored until the action finishes.
Full keyboard details are on the Accessibility tab.

sections.heading: Loading
paragraphs: While is-loading is on, a spinner replaces the leading slot and the label may stay for width stability. The button blocks repeat activation until the action resolves.

sections.heading: Color
paragraphs: Each variant and state maps to a semantic interactive token. Swatches are bound to the live tokens.

sections.heading: Typography
paragraphs: The label binds all five typography properties (family, weight, size, line height in px, letter spacing) to the label text-style tokens for its size.

sections.heading: Variants & states
paragraphs: 180 variants: Variant (4) × Size (3) × State (5) × Radius (3). The grid shows Variant × State at Size=Md, Radius=Default.

sections.heading: Focus — zoomed
paragraphs: Every variant's Focused state adds a 3px ring bound to border/interactive/focus.

sections.heading: Icons
paragraphs: Leading and trailing icon slots are 20px at Size=Md, with width bound to an icon size token. Turn them on with Has leading icon / Has trailing icon.

sections.heading: What the design system provides
paragraphs: •   A Focused state on every variant, with a 3px ring bound to border/interactive/focus.
•   A Disabled state on every variant.
•   Label typography bound to all five label text-style tokens for each size.
•   Minimum heights of 32, 40 and 48px — all above the 24×24px target-size minimum (WCAG 2.5.8).

sections.heading: Development considerations
paragraphs: •   Use a native <button> element. Default to type="button" to avoid accidental form submits; use submit or reset only when intended.
•   Disabled: use the disabled attribute or aria-disabled="true". Disabled buttons must block clicks, keypresses and focus-triggered actions.
•   Icon-only buttons need an accessible name via aria-label.
•   While loading, block repeat activation until the action resolves.
•   Never convey state through color alone.

sections.heading: Keyboard interactions
paragraphs: Moves focus to the next focusable element
Moves focus to the previous focusable element
Keyboard focus must always be visible. Pointer focus may hide the ring (focus-visible only).

sections.heading: Design recommendations
paragraphs: Automated contrast check — WCAG 2.x relative luminance (sRGB), label against the rendered button fill, for every theme combination (project-a/b × light/dark). Minimum 4.5:1 for label text (11–14px); 3:1 for disabled text (house rule TKN-005). Size=Md, Radius=Default.

Focus indicator: the ring measures 1.0–2.58:1 against the Primary and Danger fills; TKN-031 requires 3:1 against adjacent colors. Verify the ring's offset and contrast against the page surface manually.
